explain.say: That is the fundamental theorem of calculus: slope and area undo each other, like adding and taking away. Well done! Newton and Leibniz each found it in the 1600s, and it turned hard area problems into easy ones.

faq.q: What is the fundamental theorem of calculus?
faq.a: It says that differentiation and integration undo each other. If you build an area function by integrating f, its derivative is f again.

faq.q: Why does integrating speed give distance?
faq.a: Each tiny bit of time, distance grows by speed times that time, a thin strip of area under the speed graph. Adding all strips gives the total distance.
asks: Why is distance the integral of speed?

faq.q: Why does the area grow at the rate f of x?
faq.a: Move a tiny step along x and you add a thin strip of height f of x. So the area grows by f of x times the step: its rate of change is f of x.
asks: Why is the derivative of the area function f?

faq.q: How does the theorem help find areas?
faq.a: To find the area under f from a to b, find any function whose derivative is f, then subtract its value at a from its value at b. No strips needed.
asks: How do you use the fundamental theorem to find area?

faq.q: Who discovered the fundamental theorem of calculus?
faq.a: Isaac Newton and Gottfried Leibniz found it independently in the late 1600s. Earlier, Isaac Barrow and others had seen parts of the idea.

facts: The fundamental theorem of calculus links differentiation and integration as inverse processes.
Newton and Leibniz developed calculus independently in the late 17th century.

quiz.say: You integrate a function, then differentiate the result. What do you get?
quiz.show: You integrate a function, then differentiate the result. What do you get?
quiz.why: Integration and differentiation undo each other.

wrong.1: Differentiating only gives zero for a constant.

quiz.say: A car's speed is shown on a graph. What does the area under it tell you?
quiz.show: A car's speed is shown on a graph. What does the area under it tell you?
quiz.why: Area under speed against time is distance.

wrong.0: Acceleration is the slope of the speed graph, not the area.
